title: Hash Interface
concept: The Hash interface computes a hash value for a type, enabling use in HashMap, HashSet, and other hash-based data structures.
why: HashMap is the most-used collection for key-value lookups. Without Hash, your custom types can't be map keys — a critical limitation.
tips: The Hash consistency rule is critical: equal values MUST have equal hashes
Hash only the fields that determine equality — metadata can be skipped
Use #[derive(Hash)] when all fields should participate in hashing
Good hash distribution is key to HashMap performance — the default hasher handles this
common_mistakes: Breaking the Hash consistency rule — a == b but hash(a) != hash(b)
Hashing mutable fields — if the hash changes, the value is lost in the HashMap
Forgetting to hash a field that participates in PartialEq
